definitions.explanation: Behavior that violates moral principles or codes of righteousness, encompassing acts of dishonesty, betrayal, or ethical wrongdoing.
A sexual relationship outside of marriage, especially one considered morally wrong. Often found in literary and historical contexts.

examples.japanese: {不義|ふぎ}を{働|はたら}く{者|もの}は{罰|ばつ}を{受|う}ける。
examples.english: Those who commit immoral acts will be punished.

examples.japanese: どんな{理由|りゆう}があっても、{不義|ふぎ}は{不義|ふぎ}だ。
examples.english: No matter the reason, wrong is wrong.

examples.japanese: {不義|ふぎ}の{関係|かんけい}を{続|つづ}ける。
{不義|ふぎ}が{発覚|はっかく}して{家庭|かてい}が{崩壊|ほうかい}した。
examples.english: The family fell apart when the affair was discovered.

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}には{不義|ふぎ}{密通|みっつう}は{重|おも}い{罪|つみ}とされていた。
examples.english: In the Edo period, adultery was considered a serious crime.

notes:
Composed of {不|ふ} (non-, un-) and {義|ぎ} (righteousness, justice). A literary and somewhat formal word. In sense 1, it refers broadly to immoral or unjust behavior — acting against what is right. In sense 2, it specifically refers to sexual infidelity, particularly adultery, and has strong associations with historical and literary contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不義|ふぎ}を{働|はたら}く: to commit an immoral act
- {不義|ふぎ}の{関係|かんけい}: illicit relationship
- {不義|ふぎ}{密通|みっつう}: adultery (classical term)
- {不義|ふぎ}の{子|こ}: illegitimate child (archaic)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {不正|ふせい}: injustice, fraud — more modern; often used for corruption or cheating
- {浮気|うわき}: cheating, infidelity — colloquial and common in modern usage
- {不貞|ふてい}: infidelity — formal/legal term for marital unfaithfulness
